title: Yissachar of Kefar Magdi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Yerushalmi Rosh Hashanah, chapter 1, halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.1.3.4), expounding “And He saw iniquity,” etc. [Bereshit Rabbah 52:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.52.5) and [74:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.74.7) name Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Yissachar of Kefar Mandi. If so, he belonged to the second generation of the amoraim of the Land of Israel.[^1][^2]

His expositions are also mentioned in Tanchuma, Vayishlach 24 and Bamidbar 10; Vayikra Rabbah 1:13; Bamidbar Rabbah 20:3; Esther Rabbah, at the end of chapter 7; [Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Shir_HaShirim_Rabbah.2.4); and Midrash Tehillim 5:8 and 10:3.[^3]

notes.text: The printed notice has Magdi in the heading and Mandi in the body. Guggenheimer’s Rosh Hashanah has Mendi; the TE Bereshit Rabbah has Mandi at 52:5 and Magdei at 74:7. These spellings remain distinct.

Hyman’s accepted Hebrew text cites Bereshit Rabbah 52:6 and 74:6; the corresponding passages in the linked TE edition are 52:5 and 74:7. The printed second locator appears to end in ז, unlike the accepted ו. “If so” marks Hyman’s inference about generation.

The source’s פ״ב פ״ד gives chapter 2, verse 4. In the linked TE passage, Rabbi Yissachar speaks of a child’s mispronunciations of Moshe, Aharon and Ephron being accepted lovingly by God. Midrash Tehillim is the work title represented by the source’s ובמדרש ותהלים.
